headline: Result Update

highlights: Management continues to evaluate options for deploying surplus cash. • Key order wins included a 400kV generator transformer and 420kV GIS package for a 1,500MW pumped-storage project in Maharashtra, 800kV/420kV GIS for Andhra Pradesh transmission projects, 400kV reactors and 420kV/220kV GIS for a Himachal Pradesh TBCB project, and a 765kV shunt reactor for an Andhra Pradesh TBCB project.

EBITDA margin came in at 27.1%, at the higher end of the guided mid-20s band, while gross margin stood at 44.5%, with management reiterating that it does not provide gross-margin guidance given mix variability; the ₹214.4bn backlog (over 3x FY26 revenue) remains broadly stable and supports multi-year visibility, while significant HVDC execution is expected from FY28 onwards.

Overall, Q2 reflects a strong recovery in order intake and healthy execution, with the investment thesis hinging on domestic TBCB order conversion, resolution of pending RPT opportunities and the gradual ramp-up of HVDC execution from FY28.

Macro & Sector Context • Grid expansion and modernization: Management highlighted that India’s transmission sector is at an important inflection point, driven by rising electricity demand, renewable energy integration and the need for long-distance transmission infrastructure.
valuation: We maintain BUY rating on the stock with target price unchanged of ₹6,587, valuing at 55x FY29 PE.

This buy-side transaction has been executed and should not be confused with the two pending sell-side export opportunities. • Near-term order-book upside remains conditional: Conversion of the US data-centre order could provide an incremental order-intake opportunity in H2FY27.

Management expects the order booking to be significant in the relevant quarter, with execution spread over multiple years. • HVDC localization has advanced materially: Transformers, thyristor valves and controls are manufactured in India, supported by the company’s domestic engineering capabilities.

HVDC corridors are becoming increasingly important to transmit renewable power from generation centres to consumption centres. • Digitalization of the grid: Increasing grid complexity is driving demand for grid automation, real-time monitoring, predictive maintenance and software-led solutions to improve reliability and reduce AT&C losses.
